Requirements - Detailed Information
Transcripts from all Post-Secondary Institutions
You are required to upload a transcript for each institution attended. All schools at which you completed one or more full academic terms (or equivalent) should be reported on your application. This includes community colleges, summer sessions, extension programs, and any other postsecondary education for which you received credit. Do not include high schools or college preparatory schools.
The transcript legend or key for each institution (usually found on the backside of the official transcript or in the school’s general catalog or website) must be included in your uploaded document. Additional instructions can be found in the Education History section of the How to Complete the Application webpage and within the application itself.
Note: DO NOT send your transcripts or any other documents directly to UCSB unless you have been admitted and chosen to attend UCSB or you have been specifically instructed to do so. You must upload a PDF of your transcript to your application.
Letters of Recommendation
Applicants to the Ph.D. - Earth Science program are required to provide 3 letters of recommendation. General instructions can be found in the Letters of Recommendation section of the How to Complete the Application webpage and within the application itself.
Program Note on Reference Type: Academic letters preferred if available
Résumé or Curriculum Vitae
List your positions of employment or volunteer work/community service since high school, either full or part-time, including the hours per week worked and the nature and dates of employment or service.
Note: Do not include GRE scores on your Résumé or Curriculum Vitae (CV) if your program does not accept them.
Statement of Purpose
Give a brief statement outlining your reasons for undertaking a graduate program, your particular area of specialization within the major field, your past academic work, and your plans for future occupation or profession. Also include any additional information that may assist the selection committee in evaluating your preparation and aptitude for graduate study at UC Santa Barbara.
Your Statement of Purpose must be written in narrative (essay) form without duplicating content from your Personal History Statement.
Additional Program Instructions: What are the reasons you want to earn a graduate degree? Describe your current research interests and any previous research experience. Which ONE OR TWO faculty members in the department would you like to work with and why? Have you already spoken or exchanged emails with them? (We strongly encourage this.)
Note: All documents submitted as part of the application should be written solely by the applicant without the assistance of generative AI, e.g., ChatGPT. (500 words max. for the entire statement)
Personal History Statement
UC Santa Barbara is interested in a diverse and inclusive graduate student population. Please describe any aspects of your personal background, accomplishments, or achievements that you feel are important in evaluating your application for graduate study. For example, please describe if you have experienced economic challenges in achieving higher education, such as being financially responsible for family members or dependents, having to work significant hours during undergraduate schooling or coming from a family background of limited income. Please describe if you have any unusual or varied life experiences that might contribute to the diversity of the graduate group, such as fluency in other languages, experience living in bi-cultural communities, academic research interests focusing on cultural, societal, or educational problems as they affect under-served segments of society, or evidence of an intention to use the graduate degree toward serving disadvantaged individuals or populations.
A minimum word count of 250 words is required for your Personal History Statement. There is no maximum length requirement. Most statements are typically 1–2 pages. Your Personal History Statement must be written in narrative (essay) form without duplicating content from your Statement of Purpose.
Additional Program Instructions: Explain what drives your passion for Earth Science and/or research, as demonstrated by examples of personal experiences or school/community service. This may include narratives about how you overcame challenges, demonstrated resilience, or developed a unique perspective that contributes to your academic goals. If you have academic or professional experience in a field other than Earth Science, discuss how these relate to your graduate school plans.
Note: All documents submitted as part of the application should be written solely by the applicant without the assistance of generative AI, e.g., ChatGPT. (500 words max. for the entire statement)
Department Form: Supplemental Essay
Supplemental Essay
Write about as many of the topics below as are applicable to you, particularly if they were not already discussed in your personal history statement. Include labels to indicate which prompt each portion of your essay addresses. Note: All documents submitted as part of the application should be written solely by the applicant without the assistance of generative AI, e.g., ChatGPT. (1000 words max. for the entire statement)
Motivation: Describe how you tackled or overcame a challenge. What was key to your success? What strategies would you use in the future to deal with challenges in graduate school?
Creativity and problem solving: Describe a time when you applied creativity or problem solving skills to an academic assignment, research activity, or extracurricular project to achieve results that exceeded expectations.
Collegiality, collaboration, teamwork: Tell us about a time you worked as part of a team or collaboration. What role did you play? What were the challenges of working together, and how did you overcome them?
Service: If applicable, please describe any extracurricular contributions you have made to your department, community, or society more broadly, including service to disadvantaged populations.
Overcoming disadvantage: If applicable, please describe your background of persevering and succeeding despite any disadvantages that you have experienced. These could include economic or health challenges, such as being responsible for family members or dependents, having to work significant hours during undergraduate schooling, or coming from a family background of limited income. They could also include issues of identity or a struggle with feelings of belonging in academia.
Culture and perspective: If applicable, describe any uncommon or varied life experiences that might contribute to our graduate student community, such as fluency in other languages, experience living in a different culture, or interests in cultural, societal, or educational problems affecting underserved segments of society.
Writing Sample
Provide a sample of your analytical writing, such as a term paper from an Earth Science class or a report about a research project you did. Note: All documents submitted as part of the application should be written solely by the applicant without the assistance of generative AI, e.g., ChatGPT.
English Language Exam Scores (if applicable)
An excellent command of written and spoken English is required prior to enrollment at UC Santa Barbara. Applicants whose native language is not English are required to take the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL), the International English Language Testing System (IELTS), or the Duolingo English Test (DET).
Exemptions from the English language admissions requirements are permitted for applicants who have completed an undergraduate or graduate degree at an institution where the verified sole official language of instruction is English. More information can be found in the Exam Scores section of the How to Complete the Application webpage.
The minimum score requirements for accepted exams are listed below:
TOEFL Minimum Total iBT Score: 4.0 (post-January 2026) or 80 (pre-January 2026)
IELTS Minimum Overall Band Score: 7
DET Minimum Total Score: 120
